source: AitherOS/config/ecosystem.yaml (status public|no-pages), every repo and docs URL probed 200 the same day

bricks.tagline: Build AI agent fleets — 3 lines, any backend, local or cloud.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a framework's idea of how your agents should run
bricks.you_check: one loop you can read, pointed at a backend you already pay for

bricks.tagline: Portable agent skills — self-contained procedures an agent loads on demand.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that an agent knows your procedure
bricks.you_check: the procedure written down, versioned, and loadable by any agent

bricks.tagline: First-party agent packs — the ones we build, versioned and installable on their own.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that the pack you want shipped inside somebody's SDK, under whatever licence that SDK happens to carry
bricks.you_check: the pack as its own versioned artifact, with its own licence, that any agent runtime can install

bricks.tagline: A portable, scoped agent memory.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that memory stayed in its lane
bricks.you_check: tenant:user:project scopes, so a write cannot cross a boundary

bricks.install: see the repo -- Electron app (npm install && npx electron .)
bricks.tagline: Aither World Desk -- the desktop body of AitherOS Online: tray, avatars, decision cards, the Living Desktop as an overlay.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that the agent is somewhere behind a browser tab
bricks.you_check: a tray icon, a face on your desktop, and the decision card that pops when it needs you

bricks.tagline: A lightweight local gateway — bridges your apps to the AI backends you chose.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a vendor's cloud with every prompt
bricks.you_check: a local gateway routing to backends you chose

bricks.tagline: A priority-aware queue and dispatcher for agentic runs and ad-hoc CI builds. It also judges whether the runner pool is big enough for the queue it is draining, and can ask a host to grow it -- reserving capacity is zero-sum, so a saturated pool needs more of it, not a different share of it.
A semantic code graph for agents — AST + tree-sitter, call graphs.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that grep found everything
bricks.you_check: an AST + tree-sitter call graph an agent can traverse

bricks.tagline: Semantic version control on top of git — edit-ops and leases.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that no one else is editing this file
bricks.you_check: a lease, refused at commit time if you do not hold it

bricks.tagline: Anonymous multi-round expert panels — a converged answer with a trace.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: one agent's confident take on a decision
bricks.you_check: the round trace, the anonymity, and who dissents

bricks.tagline: What every tool call costs you in context, measured from your own transcripts.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that your tooling is saving you context
bricks.you_check: the measured token cost of each tool call, and what the alternative cost

bricks.tagline: Sign an artifact so a stranger can verify it.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that the artifact came from who you think
bricks.you_check: an Ed25519 seal — the key that verifies is not the key that forges

bricks.tagline: Publish an artifact and fetch it back verified.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that the download is intact
bricks.you_check: content-addressed bundles, verified on fetch

bricks.tagline: An append-only audit trail whose gaps are DETECTABLE.
Role-based access control that fails closed and explains itself.
Who is this caller? A directory and session store that fails honestly.
Reach a service that has no public address.
Prove there is a human before you let them into the nest.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that there is a person on the other end
bricks.you_check: a verdict with evidence, where "we could not tell" is not "yes"

bricks.tagline: A front gate you can put in front of anything, and hand someone the key to.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a share link anyone who sees it can use
bricks.you_check: an invitation addressed to one person, for one gate, revocable

bricks.tagline: A Linux you can hand to an agent — immutable base, capabilities included.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that the box is what you left it as
bricks.you_check: an immutable image you built, with atomic rollback

bricks.tagline: Labelled snapshots with an all-or-nothing restore.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that the restore worked
bricks.you_check: a restore that fully lands or does not land at all

bricks.tagline: Every drive on every node, indexed, classified and diffed -- so you can see what you own before you delete it.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a du you ran last month, and a peers file that says 3 TB free
bricks.you_check: an inventory snapshot per node with a diff since the last one, and each tree classified re-fetchable or not

bricks.tagline: Portable agent messaging — findings, alerts, coordination.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a SaaS in the middle of your agents
bricks.you_check: findings, alerts and coordination over your own transport

bricks.tagline: Your agent asks you a question — and acts on your answer.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that anyone read the paragraph where you asked
bricks.you_check: the ask itself, with a button that steers the session that raised it

bricks.tagline: Give an agent an email address — send, and actually receive.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a mailbox somebody else can read
bricks.you_check: mail your agents send and receive over your own server

bricks.tagline: The agentic web — agents host a mesh, and agents join one.
A portable search client — query, results, ranking.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: one vendor's idea of the web
bricks.you_check: results from whichever providers you configured

bricks.tagline: A portable browser client — navigate, console, network, DOM, screenshot.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that the page said what you were told
bricks.you_check: the render, the DOM and the requests it made

bricks.tagline: How to run a coding agent so the result survives — the laws, with evidence.
GobboNet campaigns with a real agent brain — scoped memory, graph recall.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: the model to keep a 300-message campaign coherent by itself
bricks.you_check: campaign facts recalled from scoped memory you can list and edit

bricks.tagline: Near-optimal KV cache quantization for LLM inference — sub-byte compression.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a vendor's quantisation defaults
bricks.you_check: sub-byte KV cache kernels you can benchmark yourself

bricks.tagline: Deliberately chunk artifacts into GitHub release assets — the productized aitherkvcache mirror lane.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a hand-rolled split script and a hand-edited worker manifest
bricks.you_check: byte-verified parts in a release, served with Range + CORS, sizes asserted by a live gate

bricks.tagline: PowerShell 7+ automation framework — numbered, self-describing scripts.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a pile of scripts nobody has numbered
bricks.you_check: numbered, discoverable automation with declarative playbooks

bricks.tagline: Browser extension — federated AI search, page context, and the Living OS overlay.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: what a page tells your browser to do
bricks.you_check: a federated search and desktop bridge you host

bricks.tagline: A portable reasoning client — sessions, phases, thoughts, and the chain that produced the answer.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a confident paragraph
bricks.you_check: the phases it went through, and every tool call it made to get there

bricks.tagline: Answer a question over a context far larger than the window — recursively, with the trace kept.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that everything you pasted in was actually read
bricks.you_check: which slices it opened, and what it concluded from each

bricks.tagline: Turn a failure into ranked hypotheses — and say what would confirm each one.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: the first explanation that fits
bricks.you_check: the ranked alternatives, and the observation that separates them

bricks.tagline: A REPL an agent can actually use — state that survives between turns.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: what the agent believes the value is
bricks.you_check: the value, printed from the live session

bricks.tagline: Ask a research question, get a cited report you can check.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a summary of pages nobody opened
bricks.you_check: every claim against the source it came from

bricks.tagline: See, search and steer every Claude session from one command.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: twelve terminal tabs and a bad memory
bricks.you_check: one command that names every session, finds any transcript, and opens or steers the one you want

bricks.tagline: An ARC training gym — a game a world model can watch, and six roles that play through it.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that a world model learned anything from the games it saw
bricks.you_check: transitions captured from real play, fed back, and the retrodiction score falling on grids it never saw

bricks.tagline: Predict what your environment does next, and how surprised you were.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a model because it trained without erroring
bricks.you_check: its prediction against a self-updating lookup, on the rows that are actually novel

bricks.tagline: Your terminal answers you -- type a question where a command would go.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that you already know the name of the command
bricks.you_check: what it decided your line meant, before it acts on it

bricks.tagline: The man page for the Aither World — every brick, stack and law, offline.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that the docs site is up, or that you remember the family
bricks.you_check: the whole ecosystem in your terminal, with no network at all

bricks.tagline: Train an embedding model that knows your corpus, and prove it beats the big one.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a general-purpose embedder that has never seen your code
bricks.you_check: a held-out split of whole directories, scored teacher vs student vs int8

bricks.tagline: Turn any tax PDF -- returns, W-2, 1099, statements, even scans -- into structured data you can check.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a closed tax app's sealed file you can never read again
bricks.you_check: a plain, provider-neutral schema of every figure, with the page it came from

bricks.tagline: A deterministic workflow runtime — chain agent calls with journal replay and budget control.
Your agent's permissions and config, following you to the next machine.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: that you will remember to re-approve the same thing on every box you work from
bricks.you_check: one profile, unioned rather than overwritten, with the credentials left behind

bricks.tagline: One character spec in, a rigged, animated, multi-style avatar pack out.
bricks.instead_of_trusting: a cloud 3D vendor's opaque task id
bricks.you_check: a manifest with a sha256, a licence and a rig-audit verdict per file
